config.grain_rationale: One row is one registered company name held by a company. Companies with previous names appear on multiple rows sharing the same ACN; on exactly one row per company 'Current Name Indicator' = 'Y' and 'Company Name' holds the current registered name, while on the other rows 'Company Name' holds a former registered name and 'Current Name' holds the then-current name. Because 'Current Name' carries a value only on the former-name rows, the current registered name is recoverable from BOTH row types: Company Name (when Indicator='Y') or Current Name (when Indicator is not 'Y'). Each row therefore yields at most one legal_name observation for the company; former registered names are NOT emitted as trading names (they are superseded legal names, not declared business/trading names). Per-company attributes (ACN, ABN, type, status, registration date) are identical across a company's rows and are mapped from every row.

record_id.rationale: ACN alone is not unique (471 distinct for 473 rows) because multiple name-history rows share it; ACN + Company Name gives 473 distinct values in the discovery partition, i.e. one row per company-name record and traceable back to the source.

fields.rationale: On the current-name row (Current Name Indicator='Y', 301/473 rows) 'Company Name' is the registered company name and 'Current Name' is blank. Names are space-padded to ~100 chars, hence collapse_whitespace+trim.

On rows without the current-name indicator, 'Current Name' is populated (172/473) and holds the company's current registered name, e.g. BRITAX STEELCRAFT PTY. LTD. -> BRITAX CHILDCARE PTY LTD. Verified on the header sample: rows where Indicator='Y' always have Current Name blank, and rows where Indicator is blank always have Current Name populated. The two legal_name rules are complementary, so each row emits exactly one legal_name and a company's current name is still recoverable if its Indicator='Y' row were absent from an extract.
Column 'ACN' is 9 digits on 100% of rows and passes the ACN checksum on 473/473 discovery rows; uses the acn transform, never derived from ABN.

Column 'ABN' is 11 digits on 69.3% of rows and passes the ABN checksum at exactly the same 69.3% rate; the remaining values are the literal placeholder '0' (145/473) meaning no ABN recorded, null_if'd away so the checksum transform only sees real ABNs.

Column 'Type' states the ASIC company type explicitly (APTY = Australian proprietary company 458, APUB = Australian public company 15 in discovery). APTY/APUB/FNOS/NONC are all bodies registered as companies under the Corporations Act -> 'company'. Any other code falls through to 'unknown' rather than being guessed.

Only statuses with an unambiguous ontology equivalent are mapped: REGD = registered -> active (435/473), DRGD = deregistered -> deregistered (28/473). EXAD (external administration, which may be voluntary administration or receivership rather than liquidation) and SOFF (strike-off action in progress, company still registered) have no exact enum equivalent and are deliberately mapped to 'unknown' rather than guessed.
All discovery values match shape 99/99/9999 and are day-first Australian dates (e.g. 22/12/1986); parse as %d/%m/%Y.

ASIC company type code (APTY=proprietary, APUB=public, FNOS=foreign, RACN=registrable Australian body, CCIV=corporate collective investment vehicle, NONC=no-liability). Profiled values are exactly keys of asic_company_type.
Class holds the share/guarantee structure (LMSH=limited by shares, LMGT=limited by guarantee) which entity_type flattens to 'company'. Keys match the source values; code retained in key_label.
Sub Class carries the finer ASIC structure (PROP, LIST, PSTC, LISN, ULST...). Crosswalk keys are this source's raw values; target is multi-valued so Class and Sub Class are separate observations.
entity.status is coarse and hides distress codes (EXAD external administration, SOFF strike-off). asic_company_status keys are exactly this column's values.
Column names the state register in which the company was originally registered; ext.entity.prior_registration_state is defined as exactly that and explicitly not an address.
Legacy state-registry number (shapes like C0268163E and 8-digit numerics; ACN checksum passes by chance on only 13.5%). Must not be parsed as an ACN.

On a former-name row, Company Name is the superseded legal name and Current Name is the name in force afterwards; that row's Current Name Start Date is when the later name took effect, so it dates this former name. Not a trading name.

constants.rationale: Australian register of companies incorporated under the Corporations Act (ASIC); all discovery rows are AU registrations. Asserted from metadata rather than a source column, hence moderate confidence.

unmapped.reason: Empty on 100% of profiled rows (present_rate 0.0); no data to map.

config.notes:
ZIP member COMPANY_202611.csv: UTF-8 with BOM, TAB-delimited (14 tabs/line), one header row, 15 columns. Names are space-padded to ~100 chars -> collapse_whitespace+trim. ABN uses '0' as a missing sentinel (145/473). Name-history structure: multiple rows per ACN; legal_name comes from Company Name when Current Name Indicator='Y' and from Current Name when the indicator is blank, so each row contributes exactly one current registered name and no superseded name is emitted as trading_name (entity.trading_name is intentionally not populated - this register holds no declared business/trading names). valid_from = Current Name Start Date where present, else Date of Registration. entity.status maps only REGD/DRGD; EXAD and SOFF -> unknown by design. observed_at is not stated in the file, so resource_last_modified is used. address.full/locality/postcode are not present in this source.

[ext-v1] Adds ASIC's own schema detail to the extension registry (Type -> legal_form, Class + Sub Class -> legal_form_detail as two multi-valued observations, Status -> status_detail) plus the two prior-registration columns and former legal names dated by Current Name Start Date. The record is a company (business role); this file contains no licence or premises role, so no entities/relationships are declared and no approved rule changes role or scope. Base edits are limited to removing the three ignored legacy observation.valid_* rules (7, 8, 9); index 9's Date of Deregistration remains represented by entity.status/status_detail (DRGD). All four crosswalk tables used are marked 'draft - prepared by an AI assistant' and need human verification against ASIC's data dictionary.

fields.reason: Type holds ASIC company-type codes (APTY/APUB/...) whose crosswalk keys match the profiled values; decode to legal_form is the registrar's own type, and APUB->public_company, APTY->proprietary_company in the held-out records is correct. Table is still draft/review_status unverified but the concept, keys and target enum align.

Class (LMSH/LMGT) describes share/guarantee structure, which is exactly the finer legal structure legal_form_detail is defined for; key_label output keeps code and label. Multi-valued target means a separate observation from Sub Class is acceptable. Crosswalk entries are marked unverified (LMSG/UNLM/NLIA/NONE profile coverage uncertain) but concept and keys correspond.

Sub Class values are ASIC sub-class codes, but several labels were assigned by guess and the table is explicitly draft with 'verified false' entries needing ASIC's data dictionary. The held-out output shows the concrete hazard: ULSS is labelled 'Unlisted public superannuation trustee company' and PSTC 'Proprietary superannuation trustee company' — plausible but unverified — and, more telling, PROP is decoded to 'Proprietary company', which duplicates the Type/legal-form fact rather than a sub-class, while LIST/LISN/LISS/ULST overlap with the listed/unlisted distinction of Type APUB. Mislabelled or duplicated decodes flow straight into legal_form_detail. Concept fit is acceptable; the labels are not yet trustworthy.

Status codes (REGD, DRGD, ...) are the registrar's own status, and the ontology wants the full code:label precisely so distress codes live outside the coarse entity.status enum. Status is a company-level attribute identical across rows, so attaching it to the business is correct, and nothing here emits a valid_to on a deregistered status. Table labels remain draft/unverified but the concept and key set agree with the column.

'Previous State of Registration' is a state of the original state-register incorporation (NSW/SA/VIC/QLD in the held-out rows), which the ontology defines explicitly as not an address. Emitted as a plain string on the business; no address inference is made.

'State Registration number' is the legacy state-registry number and is correctly kept as its own concept rather than parsed as an ACN or ABN. Held-out values (C0000019A, 78B00116J, 00010535, C0069532U with trailing space) are all preserved with trim/collapse and are clearly not 9-digit ACNs; null_if guards blanks.

The rule emits 'Current Name' (the later, then-current name) as ext.entity.former_name, and attaches 'Current Name Start Date' as its valid_from. That is inverted: the former name is 'Company Name' on a former-name row, and the later name's start date dates the later name, not the superseded one — a validity path belonging to a different claim. The dataset's own grain_rationale states Company Name holds the former registered name and current names are NOT emitted as trading names; yet the held-out observations show MONAKA PTY LTD, GEOFF JOHNSTON WINES PTY LTD, NIPPON LIFE INSURANCE AUSTRALIA AND NEW ZEALAND LIMITED and PETGRA PTY. LTD. emitted as 'former_name' values with the later name's commencement date. Also, the current legal_name is recovered from Company Name on the indicator='Y' row, so the same string is emitted both as legal_name (approved rule) and as a former_name here — a name cannot be both current and former. The only defensible former_name would be Company Name on non-'Y' rows, with valid_to (or nothing) rather than this valid_from.

critic.summary: Rules 0-5 are conceptually sound: Type/Class/Sub Class/Status/prior-state/prior-number all reach the right registrar concepts, prior state and prior number are correctly kept out of address and ACN handling, and Status detail correctly avoids smuggling a valid_to onto a deregistered entity. Two issues: rule 6 inverts the former-name logic — it emits the later 'Current Name' as former_name and dates it with the later name's start date (a date that belongs to a different claim), which also collides with the approved legal_name rule using the same string. Rule 2 is only doubtful: the sub-class labels are AI-guessed and unverified, decode PROP to a duplicate of legal_form, and these decodes land in legal_form_detail. No personal data or unmapped-but-clearly-relevant columns were found; 'Modified since last report' is legitimately dropped as empty.

[ext-v1] Adds ASIC's own schema detail to the extension registry (Type -> legal_form, Class + Sub Class -> legal_form_detail as two multi-valued observations, Status -> status_detail) plus the two prior-registration columns and former legal names. Fixes the critic's 'wrong' verdict: former name is Company Name on non-'Y' rows (never Current Name, which is the later name and would collide with legal_name), emitted without a validity path because Current Name Start Date dates a different claim. The record is a company (business role); no entities/relationships are declared. Base edits limited to removing the three ignored legacy observation.valid_* rules (7, 8, 9). All four crosswalk tables used are marked 'draft - prepared by an AI assistant'; the asic_company_subclass labels are AI-guessed (critic: doubtful) and need verification against ASIC's data dictionary before relying on finer sub-class detail.

fields.reason: Type values (APTY, APUB) are ASIC company type codes and decode cleanly to proprietary_company and public_company. The target is legal_form and requires a crosswalk, which is supplied. Rare values such as FNOS, RACN, and NONC are covered by the table keys, so this rule is acceptable, though the table itself is still draft.

Class (LMSH, LMGT) is genuinely ASIC's share/guarantee structure, which fits legal_form_detail. In the held-out records, LMSH produces 'LMSH: Limited by shares' and LMGT produces 'LMGT: Limited by guarantee'; both of these look correct.

Sub Class does carry finer ASIC structure, but the crosswalk labels are self-declared draft/AI-guessed. Held-out values expose this risk: PSTC is rendered as 'Proprietary superannuation trustee company' for an ordinary curtain company (TOSCA CURTAINS PTY. LTD.), and ULSS as 'Unlisted public superannuation trustee company' for AUSTRALIAN EMPLOYERS' FEDERATION LTD, which strongly suggests the subclass keys mean something else (for example, no-liability or trustee status variants). In addition, PROP is labelled 'Proprietary company', which duplicates legal_form rather than stating a finer structure. The concept fits, but the values are not trustworthy.

Status holds ASIC status codes (REGD, DRGD), and status_detail is defined as the registrar's full code and label. In the held-out records, REGD produces 'REGD: Registered' and DRGD produces 'DRGD: Deregistered'. No valid_to is attached to the deregistered record, so the rule does not violate the rule that a deregistered status carries no validity bound. Because the labels are draft, they should be verified against ASIC's help file.
Previous State of Registration names the state register of original incorporation (NSW, SA, VIC, QLD) and is explicitly not an address, which matches prior_registration_state exactly.

State Registration number holds strings such as 'C0000019A', '78B00116J', and '00010535'; they are correctly kept as a legacy registration number and are not parsed as an ACN. Whitespace trimming is applied correctly: the trailing space in 'C0069532U ' is removed.

The rule is conditional and emits Company Name as former_name only on rows where Current Name Indicator != 'Y', which is exactly the superseded-name rows in the held-out records (LOVINI before MONAKA, A.C. JOHNSTON before GEOFF JOHNSTON WINES, MLC LIFE before NIPPON LIFE). This avoids the collision with legal_name and correctly refuses to treat former names as trading names. The absence of a validity path is defensible and is stated explicitly, because Current Name Start Date dates the later name, not this one.

critic.summary: Overall the added rules are structurally sound: legal_form, status_detail, prior registration state/number, and the conditional former_name rule all mean what their canonical targets mean, and no legacy record-level validity is emitted. One real problem is rule 2: the Sub Class crosswalk labels are AI-guessed drafts, and the held-out records show suspicious decodings (PSTC and ULSS rendered as superannuation trustee company for companies that are plainly not trustees, and PROP duplicating 'Proprietary company'). The concept fits legal_form_detail, so the rule is doubtful rather than wrong, but the table should be verified against ASIC's data dictionary, and Class should be checked to see whether it alone suffices. Leaving Current Name Start Date unmapped is correct here, because no per-former-name date bound is supported. No unmapped source column clearly matches a remaining ontology target.
